name: reviewbot-notifications-off
description:
A pull request author who opted OUT of review-delivery mentions (notifications=never, saved before this session ever started). The trigger owner annotation names the author as github_user:99#user, which the AgentSession reconciler's owner_resolve links into agentsession#owner through the sole_user edge this bundle seeds directly (the harness runs no useridentity reconciler to derive it from session membership). Once claimed, the agent calls get_preferences with `user: "trigger-author"` — reading a NAMED user's preferences rather than the current turn's own author, which for a webhook-opened session has no human turn at all — and the resolved value comes back `never`, `source: user`, proving the read went through subjectresolve's sole_user resolution and the seeded user layer rather than the class default (`on_problems`). The agent honors it: the delivered review opens with the author's plain login, never a mention token.

The SAME read also proves the disclosure filter is live, not merely untested: the fixture class declares a second preference, `language`, with no visibility override (defaults to self-only) — seeded with a value for this SAME user — and it never appears in the get_preferences result at all, because a `?user-ref=` read is filtered to `visibility: class` keys BEFORE any user value is even looked up. A regression that widened the disclosure to every declared key, not just the class-visible ones, would leak `language` here and nowhere else in this bundle would catch it.
